anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
verdict: needs-work
addresses-problem: partial — the spec delivers the download, the 60s target and the empty-collection header, but it pushes the column row to mailer. That row sits under the acme/widgets group in the ticket, so the widgets CSV has no owned column contract.
findings:
- [blocker] scope @ "The CSV contains id, name, and status columns in that order. - elsewhere: acme/mailer" — this AC row sits under the `### acme/widgets` repo group in Human input, and this repo is acme/widgets. An `elsewhere:` disposition is only valid when the row sits under a group naming another repo. Mailer also cannot control which columns a widgets endpoint emits. → change the disposition to `in-scope` and specify the header `id,name,status` in that order. — probed: Human input repo-group headings vs repo acme/widgets - row is under `### acme/widgets`
- [major] gap @ Design "Column selection is assigned to mailer" — this contradicts the Goal ("delivers all four widgets rows") and Verification ("Request tests check ... column order"). The design never says which columns the endpoint writes, so nothing defines what the header-only empty export contains. → replace it with "The CSV writes columns id, name, status in that order; the header row is always written." — probed: none
- [major] gap @ Design "Export is a same-origin GET /widgets/export.csv" — the problem says users download *their* widgets, but the design gives no authentication, authorization or ownership scoping for the query ("Read widgets in id order"). As written, the endpoint could export every user's widgets. → state the auth requirement and the scoping filter (for example, widgets owned by the current user), and add a request test showing other users' widgets are excluded. — probed: none
- [minor] ambiguity @ Verification "Run the 10000-widget benchmark for the 60s row when in-scope" — the row is already marked `in-scope`, so the conditional is confusing. → drop "when in-scope" and state how the benchmark is run and asserted. — probed: none
- [minor] gap @ Verification "CSV escaping" — the Design never defines the escaping rules (quotes, commas, newlines in names), how `status` is serialized, or the line terminator. → name the escaping standard (RFC 4180), the line endings and the status representation. — probed: none
- [minor] oversimplification @ "Read widgets in id order in batches of 1000" — the design does not say whether the response is streamed as batches are read or buffered whole. That choice drives memory use and whether the 60s target is met. → state whether the response is streamed or buffered. — probed: none
lean: nothing to cut
